title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: improved params mapping (temperature/top_p/frequency/presence), role handling for system/user/assistant, support for stop sequences and logprobs in both streaming and non-streaming modes, streaming formatting improvements for function/tool calls and structured output. Backwards-compatible; minor client mapping changes documented.
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility surface fully in parity with /v1/chat.completions semantics so downstream SDKs and customers using OpenAI-compatible tooling see consistent behavior. This PR focuses on four areas: 1) params/mapping (temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens) and canonicalization to Redwood model params; 2) role semantics — ensure 'system'/'user'/'assistant' are preserved end-to-end in streaming and non-streaming paths; 3) stop sequence and logprobs — support stop sequences for both streaming and non-streaming and return token-level logprobs when requested; 4) streaming formatting and function/tool-calling — stabilize chunking and delta formatting so OpenAI-compatible clients can reconstruct messages and function call events reliably.

Summary of changes: - Add openai compatibility mapping layer: canonicalize incoming chat messages and params before routing to runtime. - Streaming runtime: emit structured deltas with explicit "role" markers and a separate "delta.function_call" envelope for tool calls; fix chunk boundary handling to avoid occasional empty-delta chunks. - Logprobs: thread optional logprobs request flag through the runtime and ensure bundles emitted in final event when streaming; non-streaming path returns logprobs in the response object consistent with OpenAI fields. - Stop sequences: early termination at runtime when stop tokens detected across prefix/kvcache boundaries; added tests for multi-token stop sequences and overlapping stop patterns. - Tests & examples: extended SDK examples (python/ts) and added e2e tests to verify parity with a reference OpenAI fixture.

Checklist: - [x] params mapping implemented and documented - [x] streaming delta format updated - [x] function/tool-calling structured events implemented - [x] stop sequence handling & logprobs supported - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] docs updated (openai_compat.md) - [x] perf smoke tests run

Testing notes: Unit tests (chat_compat/test_params.py, test_streaming_deltas.py) cover canonicalization and chunking. Integration tests run against a small local model runner; CI includes a streaming e2e job that validates reconstruction of messages and function call payloads. Perf smoke showed <3% median latency regression on typical 1-4 token responses; batching behavior unchanged. QA ran manual tests against TS/Python SDKs to ensure no behavioral regressions.

Migration notes: This is intended to be backwards-compatible for most consumers. If clients relied on earlier non-standard chunk shapes, they should update parsing to follow the documented delta envelope: each streaming chunk includes either {"delta": {"role": "assistant"}} or {"delta": {"content": "..."}} or {"delta": {"function_call": {"name":..., "arguments": ...}}} and a final {"done": true} event. The OpenAI compatibility doc includes a short section with example streaming payloads and SDK snippets.

Risk & mitigation: The largest risk was incorrect stop sequence handling across KV cache boundaries leading to premature truncation. Mitigated by adding targeted regression tests and sanity checks in the token scanner. Another risk was slight latency impact from extra envelope serialization; perf smoke tests and opt-level serialization mitigations were applied.

Related work: ENG-4821: OpenAI compatibility spec; ENG-4999: streaming stability hardening; SUP-312: customer-reported inconsistency in streaming function calls.
